text: Talk to Claude Code without making a sound. Press a button above the prompt, mouth a phrase at your webcam, press again, and the words appear in the prompt box. A lip-reading model ( Auto-AVSR ) runs locally on your Mac: no audio is recorded and no video leaves your machine. This is a prototype, and accuracy is modest. Lip reading is hard, and silent mouthing is harder than speech: expect word errors, especially on technical terms, so read the text before you send it. Claude is told which words were lip-read (with the model's other readings), so it reads them in context and asks before acting on anything destructive. Recognition uses Auto-AVSR's visual-only model vsr_trlrs2lrs3vox2avsp_base : 250M parameters, trained on 3,291 hours of video (LRS2, LRS3, VoxCeleb2, AVSpeech). ¹ Auto-AVSR model zoo : 20.3% word error rate on LRS3 (audio models: 1–2%). Why it is lower here than on the benchmark: What helps: short phrases, facing the camera in even light, mouthing a little more clearly than you would speak, and training it on your lips . Training checks how many words it gets wrong on held-out phrases, before and after, and keeps the personal model only when it gets fewer wrong, and ⚙ Settings → 🕘 History shows what the model read and what else it considered, so you can see your own accuracy. Voice dictation needs you to speak out loud. Typing needs your hands and attention. Silent dictation fits the moments in between: Install the plugin. In a terminal session of Claude Code: /plugin install lip-dictation --marketplace batanus/lip-dictation In the desktop app: click + next to the prompt box → Plugins → Add marketplace batanus/lip-dictation → Add plugin . Press 📹 Set up lip dictation above the prompt (or run /lip-setup ). It shows the download size and the model's license terms, and starts only when you press Install. Nothing needs to be installed first: setup fetches what is missing (Python, its packages, the model) into ~/.cache/lip-dictation , about 1.5 GB, with a progress bar above the prompt. If your Mac lacks Apple's Command Line Tools, their installer opens; finish it and press Set up again. Press 📹 Lip dictation , allow camera access when macOS asks (once), mouth a phrase, press ■ Stop . Requirements: macOS on Apple Silicon, a webcam, about 2.5 GB of disk, and Claude Code 2.1.287 or newer (terminal or desktop app). The first dictation of a session takes about 2 seconds to turn the camera on, while Python and the model load. After it, the next dictation is loaded ahead and waits (about 1 GB of memory, for up to 10 minutes), so the camera starts as soon as you press. The model's encoder runs on the Mac's GPU, so the text appears about half a second after you press Stop. In a terminal session, focus the button with ctrl+x then tab and press l , or bind a key to the /lip command in ~/.claude/keybindings.json : { "bindings" : [{ "context" : " Chat " , "bindings" : { "meta+l" : " command:lip " } }] } meta+l needs "Use Option as Meta key" turned on in Terminal.app or iTerm2; otherwise pick a combination that is free in your terminal. Typing /lip also works, but it replaces whatever is in the prompt box, so use the button or a key binding to add to a draft. ⚙ Settings , at the right of the row, holds everything else: Why: the stock model learned from people speaking aloud on TV and in talks. Silent mouthing moves the lips less, and everyone's lips move differently, so out of the box it makes more mistakes on you than on its benchmarks. Ten to fifteen minutes of your own phrases adapt it to you. How: press ⚙ Settings → 🎯 Train on my lips (or run /lip-train ): The phrases mix everyday English with short requests to a coding assistant, so the adapter learns your lips rather than one topic. Once trained, ⚙ Settings shows 🧠 Personal model: On . Press it to switch to the stock model ( Off ) and back, for example to compare the two in the history; training a new model switches it on. Each dictation also sends Claude the recognizer's other readings of the phrase (with the note below), since the right words are often among them. ⚙ Settings → 🕘 History opens a pane with the last dictations, newest first: the text that was inserted, the other readings the model considered, the clip length, the time it took to read, whether your personal model was used, and whether you sent the text as read or edited it first (with the prompt you sent). It is the quickest way to see what the model gets wrong for you. The same data is in ~/.cache/lip-dictation/dictations.jsonl , one JSON line per dictation or sent prompt, also printed by scripts/lipread.sh --history . ⚙ Settings → 🗑 Delete my data (or scripts/lipread.sh forget ) deletes the training phrases, the personal model and the history. The button is only shown on this computer's terminal and desktop app, never on remote surfaces such as the phone app, and /lip only starts the camera when typed here. Settings in /config : hide the button (the status line then shows the state) and turn the note to Claude off. button / /lip ──► mod (hooks/register.tsx) ──spawn──► scripts/lipread.sh ──► Lip Dictation.app ──► python -m lipread dictate │ press: go file (standby) or a new process ──────────────► camera, resampled to 25 fps │ 2nd press writes a stop file (model loads meanwhile) ◄── JSON lines: started / recording / level ×10/s / processing / result (+ other readings) (level = lip opening from MediaPipe Face Mesh, drawn as the waveform) result: $.prompt.fill inserts at the cursor; on Enter a prompt.submit hook adds a note for Claude after it: the next dictation loads ahead (`dictate --wait`) and waits for the go file sidecar/lipread/model.py : mouth crops (MediaPipe) → Auto-AVSR encoder (on the GPU) → beam search, plus the personal adapter when it is on. sidecar/lipread/personal.py : the training phrases, LoRA training of the encoder and the before/after accuracy check. scripts/camera-app/ : the helper app macOS grants camera access to (see the comment in main.c ). Each dictation is a line in ~/.cache/lip-dictation/dictations.jsonl , the History pane's source. Privacy Camera permission is granted to a small "Lip Dictation" helper app that setup builds from scripts/camera-app into ~/.cache/lip-dictation , not to your terminal or Claude. The sidecar runs through it because macOS refuses the camera without asking when the app running Claude Code declares no camera use, as under Claude Desktop. Dictation frames are kept in memory for the length of one recording and discarded; nothing is written to disk unless you pass --save to the command-line tool. Training phrases ( /lip-train ) are the exception: their mouth crops stay in ~/.cache/lip-dictation/personal/ . The history keeps the text of each dictation and of prompts that contained one in ~/.cache/lip-dictation/dictations.jsonl . ⚙ Settings → 🗑 Delete my data removes all of it. The only network access is the one-time setup: GitHub (uv, when it is not installed, and the Auto-AVSR code), PyPI (Python packages) and Google Drive (model weights). Contributing Ideas, bug reports and pull requests are all welcome: share ideas and questions in Discussions , open an issue (there is a template for sharing how well it reads your lips), or send a PR. Things that would help most: Development: claude plugin validate . and claude plugin test . check the mod, and scripts/lipread.sh check --camera checks the Python side.
